decisions.mark: states that two functions group together when their AST subtrees hash IDENTICALLY — same node kinds in the same shape — so the comparison is structural rather than textual
concludes that this catches byte-identical and RENAMED clones but is blind to near-misses — a copy with one extra statement hashes differently and does not group
states that detection is GATED behind an explicit flag rather than folded into the default recursive pass, and gives the cost reason — it is corpus-wide and needs a SECOND parse of every file
conveys that very small functions are skipped, because two single-line accessors hashing alike is not a finding
explains that a group's identity is CONTENT-DERIVED rather than positional, so a group stays comparable across runs even when files are added, removed or reordered
identifies TWO independent exclusion filters applied after grouping — a fixture-pair filter and a trivial-noise filter — and states that both default to EXCLUDING
states that the counts of what was dropped are REPORTED alongside the surviving groups rather than discarded silently
states that the fixture-pair heuristic requires at least TWO DISTINCT tags in the group, so two files under the same tag directory are not treated as a fixture pair
states that the trivial-noise rule is a CONJUNCTION — a group is dropped only when it is both small-bodied AND repeats fewer than a threshold number of times, so a widely repeated getter is KEPT
explains that the two size guards measure DIFFERENT UNITS and neither subsumes the other — a node-count floor before grouping and a line-span test after it
identifies that the textual diff against the group's first member is only computed below a size cap, and that this module performs no file I/O of its own
